correctness.rationale: Pinned the primary source to arXiv:1407.2966v1 as explicitly cited. Unlike a later version with shorter Klein coverage, v1 §4.1 pp. 9–10 actually prints all 21 line triples, the 21 quadruple and 28 triple coordinates, and the 21×49 incidence array. Independently extracted the first 21 columns and compared the 21 sorted line blocks: all agree with /workspace/reproduction/klein_check.log, whose implementation reconstructs the intersections at both roots modulo a large split prime. Since a projective equality test is a reduced linear polynomial in a with tiny integer coefficients compared to that prime, equality at both distinct roots certifies the characteristic-zero projective classes. Gévay–Pokora §2.1 independently prints the same line and point coordinates. The incidence gives 4-regularity on both parts and 84 edges; the exact characteristic polynomial has zero with multiplicity one, proving connectedness and cycle rank 43. Independently computed an exact reduced determinant of 1426415078790162284544 and modular ranks 24,34,36,35 at 2,3,7,23 respectively. The determinant exponents 18,7,5,6 with rank deficiencies 17,7,5,6 force at 2 sixteen valuations 1 and one 2, and at each other prime only valuations 1 among the nonunit local factors. Reassembling sorted valuations gives 24 units, ten 2s, 6, 138, four 966s, and 1932. This is independent of a direct Smith implementation. The stable-curve application uses a separate graph realization of rational components, four marked points each, so it is stable and has genus 43. The critical-group identification is conditional on regular semistable smoothing with unit thickness; no incorrect identification with just a partial plane blow-up is needed.
residual_risks: No assertion of an arithmetic smoothing beyond the stated conditional application; no claim about special reduction.
